title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 279
paragraphs: The Egyptians were the first to make it a point of religion not to lie with women in temples, and not to enter a temple after going in to a woman without first bathing. For almost all other men, except the Egyptians and the Hellenes, lie with women in temples and enter a temple after going in to a woman without bathing, since they hold that there is in this respect no difference between men and beasts: they point out that they see beasts and the various kinds of birds coupling both in the temples and in the sacred enclosures of the gods; and if this were not pleasing to the god, the beasts would not do so.
